s.g: The infinitive suffix for some verbs; often indicates an intransitive or perfective verb. Becomes -ать (-atʹ) after hushing consonants (ж ч ш щ) or ц. Becomes -ять (-jatʹ) after vowels. Forms both class-5 and class-1 verbs. Probably not productive in class-5 verbs except possibly for onomatopoeic verbs.
to look after, to take care of
Delhi (a megacity and union territory of India, containing the national capital New Delhi)
to stay the night, to spend the night, to stay overnight
to take to drink, to go on a drinking bout/spree
a diminutive of the female given name Ма́ша (Máša)
to refresh (also one's memory, knowledge, etc.)
to touch up (colors in a painting)
that lost good qualities; that underwent moral decline, or character decay
(of a woman) who became a prostitute
full of pathos, impassioned, passionate, emotional, pathetic
a person living at someone else's expense; dependent, parasite, leech
to take off one’s clothes, to undress, to disrobe, to get undressed
a lubricant made of minerals or plants
icy slush that flows down the river before the river freeze
a place in a game of lapta where the ball is hit and thrown
tower, tower-room; a living area in a building or upper part of a building in the shape of a tower, especially in ancient Rus.
used to link a noun with a relative clause, as in the following constructions; usually translated as "the" or, additionally in the plural, "those"
the other, the opposite, the distant, the far (side etc.)
Used in certain collocations to emphasise contrast with something else.
that one, those ones (something distal to an observer)

used to refer to the instance / instances of the noun in question or just spoken about, or, with кто (kto), the person/people, that fall(s) into a particular category — that, the one; in the plural: those, the ones

used to refer to the instance / instances of the noun in question or just spoken about, or, with кто (kto), the person/people, that fall(s) into a particular category — the person, the guy/girl/etc.; in the plural: the people etc.

used to refer to any instance / instances of the noun in question or just spoken about, or, with кто (kto), any person/people, that fall(s) into a particular category — one; in the plural: those, ones

used to refer to any instance / instances of the noun in question or just spoken about, or, with кто (kto), any person/people, that fall(s) into a particular category — someone, a person, anyone, whoever; in the plural: those, (the/those) people, anyone, whoever, some (people)

used to refer to the kind/sort/type of the noun in question or just spoken about, or, with кто (kto), person/people, described in the following clause — the kind/sort/type (of [noun]), the kinds/sorts/types (of [noun in plural])

used to refer to the kind/sort/type of the noun in question or just spoken about, or, with кто (kto), person/people, described in the following clause — the kind/sort/type of person/people, the type (to), one(s) (to)

Optionally used in the following construction to refer to the person denoted by кто (kto) earlier in the sentence. Can be omitted, and in English usually the sentence is translated without it too. Has the meaning "that person".
Used to refer to the last-mentioned person in a sentence; usually simply translated with the relevant pronoun or the person's name/role. Has the meaning "the latter".
Used in certain collocations to emphasise contrast with something else.
the wrong one, not the right one, wrong
The elongated fabric that is drawn behind a bride’s gown, train
